pairs.question: Macedones de te iudicaturi sunt: quaero, an patrio sermone sis apud eos usurus?
pairs.answer: Praeter Macedonas plerique adsunt, quos facilius quae dicam percepturos arbitror, si eadem lingua fuero usus qua tu egisti, non ob aliud, credo, quam ut oratio tua intellegi posset a pluribus.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange (sect. IX/X boundary). The king genuinely asks Philotas whether he will use his native (Macedonian) tongue before the assembly; setup 'Macedones de te iudicaturi sunt' is kept so 'apud eos' has a referent. Dropped speech tags 'inquit' (king's) and 'Tum Philotas: inquit'. Answer is Philotas's first sentence to the first full stop, in which he indicates he will use the common language because more bystanders will understand; cut there, before the next sentence ('Tum rex: Ecquid videtis...') where the king resumes.
